subject: Praxis Order Form - output & model-training rights clarification
messages:
From: Anna Morales <anna@praxishealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@praxishealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-05T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Order form questions: output ownership & training rights

Hi Logan —

Thanks for sending the draft order form earlier today. Our legal and product teams reviewed and surfaced a couple of items we need clarified before procurement can approve:

1) Output ownership: the MSA/Order Form implies Praxis will own the "Outputs" generated by the models used by our product. We want explicit confirmation that downstream ownership (including distribution to our customers) is permitted and that Redwood will not assert ownership over customer-facing outputs.

2) Training / data use: Section 7 currently grants Redwood broad rights to use customer content for model improvement. Given our regulated dataset and PHI concerns, we need either (a) a carve-out that forbids using any customer content for model training without a separate opt-in agreement, or (b) a narrow telemetry/feedback license that is limited to aggregated, de-identified usage metrics for performance tuning with strict retention windows.

3) Feedback license: Could you confirm whether the standard feedback license below requires a royalty-free assignment, or whether it can be limited to a license solely for improving "service performance" with no productization or resale rights?

We attached our redlines (Praxis_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf) with inline comments. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through. Marcus — copying procurement to keep them in the loop.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Morales
Senior Counsel, Praxis Health
anna@praxishealth.com

Quick summary of next steps from our side:

- Ben and I can host a 30-minute call with you + Marcus to align on acceptable clause language to keep procurement moving.

Preliminarily: Redwood's intent is not to claim ownership of your product outputs delivered to end customers. The broader training clause exists to support model quality across our hosted customers, but I appreciate the sensitivity for regulated data.

I'll hold a proposed slot tomorrow 11:00–11:30 PT — does that work for you? Attached is a quick summary we plan to circulate internally (praxis_redlines_summary.xlsx).

Subject: Re: Order form questions: output ownership & training rights

Anna — Laura from Legal at Redwood here. Thanks for the redlines; I reviewed the attached PDF and outline our position below. I copied Ben for commercial context.

1) Output ownership
- Position: We are comfortable (and commonly provide) a clause that confirms the customer owns Outputs they receive from the service for their internal use and distribution to their customers, subject to any third-party content obligations. We will not claim ownership of customer Outputs.
- Proposed language: "Customer owns all Outputs generated solely from Customer Content and Customer prompts. Redwood retains no ownership rights in such Outputs."

2) Training / data use
- Position: We aim to be able to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry to improve model performance. However, we understand Praxis's regulatory constraints. We can offer two options:
  a) Default: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified usage data for service improvement; no customer-identifiable data will be used for model training. Retention limited to 90 days for telemetry used in tuning.
  b) Opt-in: If Praxis opts in, we can offer a paid add-on that allows use of customer data for supervised model training under enhanced controls (isolated dataset, longer retention, audit access).
- We will not use content that contains PHI or specially-protected categories for any model training unless explicitly agreed in a separate secure SOW.

3) Feedback license
- Position: We can narrow the feedback license so it is limited to a royalty-free, non-exclusive, worldwide license "solely to improve and operate the Redwood service and not for independent commercialization or resale."

I've attached a marked-up excerpt of the MSA/Order Form with suggested language inline (see attached). If the above aligns, Ben and I suggest a short call tomorrow to finalize language (30 minutes). If you prefer written redlines, we'll circulate a revised draft by EOD.

Regards,
Laura Bennett

laura@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Order form questions: output ownership & training rights

Laura — thank you for the clear options, that helps a lot. A few follow-ups from our side after speaking with product: 

- Output ownership language proposed is acceptable, but Praxis needs an explicit statement that Praxis may sublicense Outputs to downstream customers and partners. Please add "including the right to sublicense to end customers and partners" to the Outputs clause.

- For the training/data use: option (a) (aggregated, de-identified telemetry only, 90-day retention) is close to what we need, but we require guaranteed deletion of any logs that contain customer identifiers and confirmation that any aggregated datasets used for tuning will be sampled across downstream customers (no single-customer model footprints).

- Feedback license: Praxis will accept the narrowed feedback license provided you add an explicit prohibition on using feedback to create a for-sale derivative product ("no commercialization").

We are available for the call tomorrow 11:00–11:30 PT. Marcus will lead procurement questions.

Best,
Anna

Subject: Re: Order form questions: output ownership & training rights — agreed path

Anna / Marcus / Procurement team — thanks for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and agreed path so procurement has everything in one thread: 

1) Outputs: Redwood will update the Order Form to include: "Customer owns all Outputs generated solely from Customer Content and Customer prompts, including the right to sublicense Outputs to end customers and partners. Redwood retains no ownership rights in such Outputs."

2) Training / data use: Redwood will adopt option (a) with the following explicit commitments:
  - Only aggregated, de-identified telemetry will be used for service improvement.
  - Any logs containing customer identifiers will be deleted within 7 days unless a separate retention agreement is signed.
  - Any dataset used for tuning will be sampled across customers to avoid single-customer model footprints.
  - No PHI or protected-category content will be used for training without a separate opt-in SOW.

3) Feedback license: Language will be narrowed to: "Customer grants Redwood a royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use Feedback solely to improve and operate the Redwood service; Redwood will not commercialize or resell Feedback as a product."

4) Next steps:
  - Laura will produce heavily redlined Order Form for signature (target: 2028-07-09 EOD).
  - Ben will issue a commercial summary for procurement (pricing/term impacts of opting into training) and route to procurement@praxishealth.com.
  - Logan to circulate final DocuSign link once Legal confirms the redline.

Please reply if this record omits anything substantive. Assuming no further changes, we'll prepare the final Order Form and DocuSign packet and copy procurement on the envelope.

Thanks — appreciate the collaborative approach.
